subject: ventures/garmin-world-traveler-watchface
professional: a Garmin Connect IQ watch-face developer who ships to the Connect IQ Store, with a time-zone/tzdata specialist as second reader: first checks are that the build compiles and renders legibly on round and small displays, that every shown city's offset matches tzdata at DST edges, and that the tests exercise the code that actually ships on the watch

evidence.correctness: Monkey C compiler is not installed (`which monkeyc` printed nothing; the README itself says the SDK is not available), so the shipped .mc code was never executed and the rubric cap of 2 applies. Instead I recomputed outputs from a source the author did not write. `node --test test/citydata.test.mjs`: 3 tests pass (4.7 s). I then wrote my own Python checker (scratchpad gw.py) that parses the 42-city table out of source/CityData.mc and re-derives DST from the legal rule definitions using absolute instants (US 2nd Sun Mar 02:00 standard to 1st Sun Nov 02:00 daylight; EU last Sun Mar/Oct 01:00 UTC; AU 1st Sun Oct 02:00 std to 1st Sun Apr 03:00 daylight; NZ last Sun Sep 02:00 std to 1st Sun Apr 03:00 daylight), not the .mc's month/day/hour integer keys, and compared against Python zoneinfo (system tzdata) for all 42 cities every 15 minutes from 2023-01-01 to 2040-01-01 (25,034,688 samples): 0 mismatches. Spot values agree with hand knowledge: New York 2026 DST ends 2026-11-01 06:00 UTC, London 2026 starts 2026-03-29 01:00 UTC, Sydney 2026 ends 2026-04-05 16:00 UTC. Run over 2000-2022 the same checker finds divergences (e.g. Mexico City, Istanbul, Moscow, Sao Paulo, Fiji, Caracas) which are historical rule changes the face does not claim to model. Independent recompute of label placement (scratchpad col.py): for every day of 2026 I computed each city's true offset from zoneinfo and its angular slot mod 24 h; 8 pairs of cities that share a label ring land on exactly the same angle for months of the year (see defects), so the drawn output is wrong for those cities even though the offsets are right. Not verified: Gregorian.moment/utcInfo/day_of_week semantics, drawing, fonts, any device behaviour.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked by reading source (none could be run or rendered): 42-city table with two rings (CityData.mc, 42 rows, test asserts 42 unique abbreviations: present); fixed 24 h ring with ticks and 3-hourly numbers (drawHourRing: present); per-city angle from own local hour (drawCityRing: present); now-marker (drawNowMarker: present); big digital time honouring is24Hour (formatTime: present, 12 h shows A/P suffix); date line (drawCenter: present); night-tinted ticks (isNight: present, though the hour numbers 0, 3, 6, 18, 21 are always white so the tint only reaches ticks); four themes via settings.xml/properties.xml (present, Themes.get wraps invalid indexes); no permissions (manifest has no iq:permissions: true); DST for US/EU/AU/NZ (verified numerically above). Claim 'same-offset pairs so they do not overlap' holds for standard offsets only (see defects). Never done: no compile, no simulator screenshot (README admits docs/design-mockup.png is a mock rendered outside the simulator), no store listing (site says prototype), the device list in manifest.xml was never validated against an SDK (README says to refresh it first). Roadmap items (AOD, day/night arc, tap highlight, localisation) are honestly listed as not done. Because nothing was ever built or rendered, end-to-end completeness is unproven.
evidence.verification: Ran `node --test ventures/garmin-world-traveler-watchface/test/citydata.test.mjs`: pass 3, fail 0. The test PARSES the city table from CityData.mc but the DST rule functions (isDstUs/Eu/Au/Nz, nthSundayOfMonth, effectiveOffsetSeconds) are a hand-copied JS port inside the test file, so editing the real .mc rules cannot fail it. Seeded three one-line mutations in source/CityData.mc, each followed by the test and `git checkout source/CityData.mc`: (a) isDstUs November end key `keyOf(11, endDay, 1, 0)` changed to `2` (this is exactly the bug VENTURE.yaml says was fixed on 2026-08-21): 3/3 pass, NOT caught; (b) isDstAu start key `keyOf(10, startDay, 2, 0)` changed to `startDay + 7` (AU DST starts a week late): 3/3 pass, NOT caught; (c) New York :offset -5*3600 changed to -6*3600 (a table error): 1 pass 2 fail, CAUGHT. So the test guards the table and the idea of the rules, not the code that runs on the watch. The hourly sampling over 2025-2027 is good at transition edges; the VENTURE.yaml note that 'no test harness exists' is stale. The only CI workflow (garmin-world-traveler-watchface-ci.yml) only XML-parses manifest/resources and its path filter does not include source/ or test/, so the node test never runs in CI (grep of .github/workflows finds no reference to citydata.test). No test covers the view, themes, formatTime or the label-collision geometry.
evidence.craft: Read in full: source/CityData.mc (244 lines), WorldTravelerView.mc (214), Themes.mc, WorldTravelerApp.mc, manifest.xml, resources/settings/*.xml, test/citydata.test.mjs, the CI workflow. Good: small, readable, comments explain the legal basis of each DST rule and the 01:00-standard subtlety; offsets stored as standard time plus a symbolic rule; Themes.get guards negative and out-of-range indexes; everything is derived from screen size; no permissions. Defects: onLayout/onShow/onHide/onExitSleep/onEnterSleep are empty stubs; `Properties.getValue` has no guard for a missing key beyond a null check (acceptable) and the theme lookup and Properties read happen on every draw; localInfoAt calls Gregorian.moment up to 3 times per city per draw (42 cities) with no caching, fine at one draw per minute but wasteful on battery; lastSundayOfMonth takes a caller-supplied daysInMonth (works only for the two non-February months used); keys compare month/day/hour/minute within one year, so the AU/NZ wrap logic relies on `||`; stale text: properties.xml comment says 'ring of 24 world-city zones', WorldTravelerApp.onSettingsChanged comment mentions 'city selections' that do not exist; the test duplicates the engine in a second language (two copies to keep in sync, with nothing enforcing it). Label strings: abbreviation IST means Istanbul here but is the common code for India Standard Time, LAS is Las Vegas airport, but also commonly read as Los Angeles or Lisbon, MOW/PEK/TYO mix IATA city codes and are unfamiliar to many users.
evidence.claims: Checked each: (1) '42 cities' backed by the table (42 rows, test asserts it). (2) 'UTC-11 through UTC+12 plus UTC+5:30': backed. (3) 'No permissions, no network': manifest.xml has none: backed. (4) 'Automatic, self-contained DST for US, EU, Australia, New Zealand': numerically backed by my zoneinfo comparison 2023-2040. (5) 'two label tiers so same-offset pairs do not overlap': true for standard offsets only; across the year 8 same-ring pairs coincide exactly for 183-238 days of 2026 (PPG/AKL, SYD/HIR, MEL/NOU, DEN/MEX, NYC/CCS, AZO/REY, PAR/JNB, ATH/IST) and KHI/DEL/DAC sit 7.5 degrees apart on one ring; the README's own explanation of the ring split is therefore incomplete and the test named 'same-offset cities never share a label ring' tests only standard offsets. (6) README 'Live page https://marisstella.app/garmin-world-traveler-watchface/': not loaded here (proxy), site/index.html exists. (7) llms.txt links https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/... (the retired GitHub Pages host that now only redirects per CLAUDE.md) as 'The tool', and carries the boilerplate 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial...' which does not fit a watch face. (8) VENTURE.yaml says 'no test harness exists for Monkey C in this repo' while README and test/ describe one (stale). (9) The README 'It caught two wrong cities (Cairo ... Santiago)' is a history claim I could not check, but the replaced cities are correct now. (10) site/index.html honestly says Prototype, not on the Store, demand untested, and carries disclaimer and no-warranty text; the README's screenshot is labelled a mock-up, not a capture. (11) manifest device ids (e.g. fenix7spro, descentmk3_51mm, vivoactive5) were not validated against any SDK; README says so.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through, by reading: a frequent traveller wants to read the time in several cities at a glance. They must install the Connect IQ SDK, generate a developer key, build, sideload (README steps; no .prg, no store listing, none of it tried here). Once installed, the face shows 42 three-letter labels in FONT_XTINY on two radii; no city is highlighted or selectable (tap highlight is on the roadmap), and the list is not configurable without editing source. In the maths of the angles, each city's slot moves with its own local hour, so a user has to read city codes against a 24-hour ring, mentally. For about half the year, eight pairs of labels are drawn on top of each other (e.g. NYC over CCS, PAR over JNB, SYD over HIR through the northern summer or southern summer), and KHI, DEL and DAC overlap at 7.5 degrees apart on every day. Real legibility on a 240 px MIP screen was never checked (no render exists). With no build, no render and no outside user, a traveller cannot rely on it today.
evidence.domain: Compared against how a tz specialist and a horologist would approach this. DST: hand-rolling five symbolic rules instead of a tz database is a defensible choice on Connect IQ, the legal bases are right and match tzdata for 2023-2040 in every city sampled; limits (no Southern Hemisphere rules other than AU/NZ, and cities whose governments change rules go stale, which the code comments admit) are disclosed. Worldtimer design: a real worldtimer bezel has a fixed city ring and a moving 24 h ring so two cities in the same zone naturally share a slot; this face inverts that, so cities move across the ring and DST shifts make different-zone cities collide, a thing a mechanical bezel would not do. The design guards only against collisions at standard time. A horologist or Connect IQ reviewer would also ask for AOD/low-power behaviour (listed as roadmap, not done) and a legibility pass on real devices. A tz specialist would also note tests that run the shipped code, not a port, are the norm.

defects.what: Label collisions: 8 pairs of cities drawn on the same ring land on exactly the same angle for 183-238 days of 2026 once DST shifts one of them (NYC/CCS, DEN/MEX, PAR/JNB, ATH/IST, AZO/REY, SYD/HIR, MEL/NOU, PPG/AKL), so two 3-letter labels print on top of each other, and KHI/DEL/DAC (outer ring, 7.5 degrees apart) overlap every day. The README and test claim same-offset pairs never overlap but check only standard offsets. Computed with zoneinfo offsets for each day of 2026 (scratchpad col.py); not seen on a screen.
defects.where: ventures/garmin-world-traveler-watchface/source/CityData.mc:44-92 (:ring assignment), source/WorldTravelerView.mc:130-148; test/citydata.test.mjs 'same-offset cities never share a label ring'

defects.what: The test does not exercise the code that ships: the DST functions are a JS copy inside the test, and seeded mutations to the real isDstUs end key (the exact bug VENTURE.yaml says was fixed) and isDstAu start key both passed 3/3. Only table edits are caught.

CI never runs the node test (the workflow's paths are manifest.xml and resources/** only and it only XML-parses) and nothing compiles the Monkey C, so a syntax error in any .mc file would merge green.

The face was never built or rendered: no simulator screenshot exists (only a mock-up), device ids in manifest.xml were never validated against an SDK, and FONT_XTINY legibility with 42 labels on small round screens is untested.
llms.txt points at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host and uses the calculator boilerplate ('numbers typed in, not legal, tax...').

Stale text: VENTURE.yaml says no Monkey C test harness exists; properties.xml comment says '24 world-city zones'; WorldTravelerApp comment mentions 'city selections'; night tint does not apply to the hour numbers (always white).

Ambiguous city codes: IST for Istanbul (conventionally India Standard Time, and Delhi/Mumbai are also on the face), LAS for Las Vegas, MOW, PEK and TYO are non-obvious to most travellers; the face has no legend.

verdict: A small, tidy, well-commented prototype whose time-zone maths is right: my independent legal-rule checker agrees with Python zoneinfo for all 42 cities across 25 million 15-minute samples from 2023 to 2040, and the author's own node test passes. It does not meet the bar. The Monkey C was never compiled or rendered (no SDK here, none ever used in CI), so correctness is capped at 2. The one test checks a JS copy of the DST rules, so two seeded mutations in the real rule code survived (one of them the very bug the venture notes say was fixed), and CI does not run that test at all. Independently of the code, the label layout is wrong for months of the year: eight pairs of cities land exactly on top of each other once DST shifts one of them, and Karachi, Delhi and Dhaka overlap daily, contradicting the README's claim that the two rings prevent overlap. The honest status labelling (prototype, not on the Store, mock-up clearly marked) is a strength. Scores reflect only what I ran: the node test, my Python recomputations and three mutations; I could not run the Monkey C, load the live page, or see any rendering. Cheapest fixes: make the test load and run the .mc rules (or transpile them), run it in CI, and assign rings per time-of-year (or a third ring/angle nudge) so colliding pairs separate.
